previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a right-handed male with composite Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted electively for his eighth cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He reported feeling well aside from a persistent floater in his left eye, which remained stable. He received methotrexate on day one with leucovorin rescue and aggressive IV hydration to maintain urine pH above 8.0. His renal function remained stable, though liver enzymes transiently elevated and subsequently trended downward. A brain MRI showed no new lesions or tumor recurrence, consistent with prior findings. His aspirin was restarted during admission. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue home medications and follow up for his next chemotherapy cycle in December.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Hodgkin's lymphoma, for methotrexate infusion.  Please evaluate
brain lymphoma.

___ and ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted brain imaging, including
diffusion-weighted imaging, and gadolinium-enhanced post-contrast imaging.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of mass, mass effect, or infarction.  No
diffusion abnormality is detected.  There is no abnormal enhancement after
contrast administration.

Small T2 hyperintense focus in the left posterior frontal lobe, with tiny
areas of susceptibility consistent with old blood products from prior biopsy
is slightly decreased in size since prior exam of ___.  Left parietal burr
hole is unchanged.

Few scattered foci of subcortical white matter FLAIR signal hyperintensities
are unchanged, most consistent with chronic small vessel ischemic disease.
Ventricles and sulci are normal and unchanged from prior exam.

IMPRESSION:  Little change in appearance of the brain from prior exams, with
slightly decreased size of small T2 hyperintensity in left posterior frontal
lobe, most likely representing gliosis.  No abnormal enhancement.
